title.narrative: Lao PDR Global Partnership for Education III: Learning and Equity Acceleration Project

description.narrative: The Lao PDR Global Partnership for Education III: Learning and Equity Acceleration Project (GPE III – LEAP) is financed by a mix of World Bank IDA (US$47.4 million, including the additional US$17.4 million) and GPE grant (US$16.9 million). The Additional Financing (AF) extends the project's implementation period from May 31, 2027, to May 31, 2029, to consolidate and expand achievements in improving learning outcomes and strengthening education systems. The theory of change underlying the components remains centered on three key hypotheses: (1) For schools to produce learning, they need prepared, present and motivated learners who have supportive learning environments before starting Grade 1; (2) For students to learn, they need teachers who are present, motivated, and equipped with adequate content knowledge and pedagogic skills; and (3) Teachers need strong school systems with supportive management, adequate resources, parental engagement, and routine professional management. The project continues with the same three components, now expanded through the AF: Component 1: Prepared and Motivated Learners - Significantly expanded with additional Community Child Development Group (CCDG) shelters (increased from 245 to 305), enhanced Multi-age Teaching (MAT) program (expanded from 262 to 394 schools), extended Reading Readiness Program (RRP) with new read-at-home activities, and expanded National School Meals Program (NSMP) covering 190 additional schools. Component 2: Prepared and Motivated Teachers - Maintained at current scope to consolidate gains in teacher professional development and allocation initiatives.Component 3: Effective Governance for Improving Teaching and Learning - Enhanced with an increased budget allocations up to US$10,000 per district annually to 40 priority districts to support activities financed by the project at the local level. Allocations will be transferred gradually, based on the assessment of needs and capacity. The AF emphasizes deepening impact within existing target areas rather than expanding to new provinces, focusing on the 40 priority districts identified by the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES). It incorporates sustainability features including community-based approaches, climate-resilient infrastructure improvements, and pilot approaches for transitioning program financing. Components 2 and 3 continue to use both traditional expenditure-based financing and a result-based financing approach using performance-based conditions, while Component 1 uses traditional expenditure-based financing. The project remains aligned with the Government of Lao PDR's Education and Sports Sector Development Plan and the World Bank Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for Lao PDR (FY2023-FY2026).
To improve learning outcomes in primary grades in target districts and strengthen teacher and system performance in Lao PDR.

condition.narrative: Annual Work Plans and BudgetsFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.CRecurrent, AnnualThe Recipient, through MOES, shallprepare and furnish to the Association for its no-objection no later than December 1 of each year an annual work plan and budgetduring the implementation of the Project containing relevant Project activities and expenditures proposed to be included in theProject in the following fiscal year, including a specification of the sources of financing.

CCDG Grants and School Block GrantsFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.DThe Recipient, through MOES, shall prepare andfurnish the Financing proceeds available to eligible CCDGs and Selected Schools in accordance with the guidelines, procedures andcriteria set forth in the Project Implementation Manual and the additional terms and conditions acceptable to the Association.

Environmental and Social Safeguards Financing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.GRecurrent, Continuous The Recipient, throughMOES, shall (i) ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards and the ESCP(including the management tools and instruments referred to therein) in a manner acceptable to the Association, and (ii) not amend,abrogate, repeal, suspend or waive any of their provisions unless the Association agrees otherwise, and report on their status ofimplementation as part of the project reports.

Grant Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.B.2Recurrent, Continuous/ Due date: March 31 annuallyThe Recipient, through MOES, shallfurnish reports to the Association on the status of achievement of the relevant PBC Targets.

Institutional Arrangements Financing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.ARecurrent, ContinuousThe Recipient, through MOES, shallmaintain, throughout the Project implementation period, the Project Advisory Council, Project Steering Committee, and EducationCoordination Unit; all with functions, staffing and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Mid-term ReviewFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section II.BOnce, 30 months after the Effective DateObligation of theRecipient, through MOES, to prepare and furnish to the Association a mid-term report in form and substance satisfactory to theAssociation.

Performance-based Condition Monitoring and Reporting Grant Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.B.1 Recurrent, Continuous/ Due date:the appointment of an Independent Verification Agency to carry out independent verification of the status of achievement of PBCtargets from six (6) months after thirty (30) months after the effective date. The rational is that the Independent VerificationAgency is not needed until the 4th years target for PBC 3.

Project Implementation ManualFinancing Agreement: Schedule 2, Section I.BRecurrent, ContinuousThe Recipient, through MOES,shall carry out the Project in accordance with the Project Implementation Manual (including the sub-manuals governing the provisionof CCDG Grants and School Block Grants), and not amend, waive or abrogate any provisions of the manual unless the Associationagrees otherwise in writing.
